GCSE Results
*From September 2026, senior girls will be educated at the combined Senior School on the St Teresa’s site.
Exam Results 2025
Over half of all GCSE grades awarded were at 9 to 7, the highest possible grades, with an impressive 38% at grade 9 alone. One in five of the total 422 grades achieved was a 9.
There were many exceptional individual achievements, including one student securing grade 9 in all 11 of her subjects, and another earning 10 top-grade 9s.
We are especially proud of our “value added” results. Independently produced data shows that, on average, Manor House students outperformed their peers, achieving 1.3 grades higher in every subject compared to students of a similar ability nationwide.
(Source: Centre for Evaluation and Monitoring).

Our Setting
Our private Surrey Nursery School is ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate) registered. We have our own Forest School and purpose-built Early Years facilities. These include two wonderful play areas; an outdoor all-weather playground which includes sand and water play, climbing frames, a sensory kitchen and a train, and an Orchard garden which contains our much-loved pirate ship and larger play equipment, which nursery children share with the older children.
Our outstanding, purpose-built classrooms are located in a quiet, secure area of the school and provide a happy, dedicated environment for your child. Children have access to stimulating activities throughout the day both indoors and outdoors in our safe outdoor learning environment. Children enjoy the freedom of being able to take their learning outdoors and explore the environment around them.
Alongside our specialist Nursery area, children benefit from weekly Forest School sessions in The Dell – an outdoor classroom set amidst our extensive grounds where the children can explore and engage in nature walks and practical learning activities. Our outdoor learning facilities support the children in their development by giving them opportunities to explore the natural world around them and challenge themselves further than they can in the classroom.
Our open, bright and spacious classrooms are the perfect environment for children to thrive in. Each room has a role play corner for the children to explore their imaginations, a book corner where the children can find a quiet space to look through a story, and a construction zone to allow for creativity. The classrooms are filled with resources and toys for the children to explore daily which are tailored to children’s interests and the half termly topic. We ensure that throughout play, children are having access to educational toys and resources.
We endeavour to make all children feel happy and safe at Manor House School.

Manor House School Open Morning Showcases Outstanding Education in Surrey
Posted: 18th August 2026
Families searching for an exceptional independent school in Surrey are warmly invited to attend the Manor House School Nursery and Prep School Open Morning on Friday 2 October, from 9.30am to 12.20pm.
Located in Bookham, Surrey, Manor House School is a leading independent school for girls, offering a nurturing and ambitious educational environment from Nursery through to Year 6 in the Prep School. This special 'School at Work' Open Morning provides prospective families with the opportunity to experience the school in action, meet the Head, teachers and pupils, and discover what makes Manor House School such a popular choice for families across Surrey.
Visitors will enjoy guided tours of the school, including its refreshed facilities and impressive new Dance Studio, while learning more about the academic, creative and sporting opportunities available to pupils. Families considering a Nursery in Surrey or a girls' Prep School in Surrey will gain valuable insight into the supportive and inspiring environment that helps every child thrive.
Manor House School also offers a welcoming co-educational Lower Prep, creating a strong foundation for children before progressing into the School's highly regarded girls' education pathway.
Click here to register for Open Morning.
As part of the Effingham Schools Trust (EST), Manor House School benefits from being part of a family of schools that includes Cranmore School, St Teresa's School and Effingham Sixth Form. Together, the Trust provides a seamless educational journey from Nursery through to Sixth Form.
United by the ethos "Large enough to challenge. Small enough to care.", the Trust combines academic excellence, outstanding pastoral care and exceptional opportunities for every pupil. EST's successful Diamond Model offers co-educational learning in the early years, single sex education from Years 3 to 11, and a co-educational Sixth Form experience, providing the benefits of both focused learning and collaboration.
Across the Trust, pupils benefit from small class sizes, specialist teaching, excellent wellbeing support and an extensive co-curricular programme. For families looking for a leading independent school in Bookham or a girls' school in Surrey, the Manor House School Open Morning is the perfect opportunity to discover a school where children are known, valued and inspired to achieve their best.

Year 6 Enjoy #UnforgettableExperiences on Isle of Wight Residential
Posted: 3rd June 2026
Our Year 6 pupils recently returned from an exciting three-night residential trip to Little Canada on the Isle of Wight, where they took part in a wide range of outdoor adventures with PGL. The visit was a fantastic opportunity for the girls at our independent school for girls in Surrey, to develop independence, resilience and teamwork, while creating lasting memories with their friends.
During their stay, the girls embraced every challenge with enthusiasm. Kayaking on the Solent was a particular highlight, as they learned new skills and took part in fun games on the water. On land, they demonstrated great courage tackling the zip wire and trapeze, pushing themselves beyond their comfort zones and supporting one another every step of the way.
The programme also included a variety of problem-solving activities, encouraging the girls to think creatively and work collaboratively. One of the most memorable experiences was the ‘Survivor’ challenge, where they built shelters in the woods and learned practical skills such as preparing wood and using flints to start a fire.
There were plenty of opportunities for friendly competition too, from climbing challenges against the clock to archery contests aiming for the highest score. Aeroball, a lively mix of basketball and volleyball on a trampoline, proved to be a firm favourite.
In the evenings, the girls enjoyed relaxing together, playing card games and unwinding after busy days, before settling in for a good night’s sleep.
Throughout the trip, the girls were excellent ambassadors for the school. Their positive attitude, teamwork and willingness to try new things made the residential a resounding success and a truly #UnforgettableExperiences for all involved.

Nursery & Kindergarten
Introducing our Director of Nursery Education
Ms M Luke, NVQ 3, BA Hons
Nursery
Welcome to Manor House Nursery School (Pre-School), our Nursery in Surrey. Based in Bookham, near Leatherhead in Surrey and set amidst the grounds and facilities of Manor House School, Bookham.
Manor House School Nursery has just been awarded the ‘Top 20 Recommended Nursery School’ Award by www.daynurseries.co.uk. This means we were one of the most recommended Nursery Schools in the South East in 2023 based on over 50,000 published reviews.
Our parent testimonials are testament to our current 10/10 star rating. Here are a few quotes from our recent reviews:
What Makes Manor House Nursery & Kindergarten a Top-Ranked Early Years School?
Our Nursery and Kindergarten Classes are perfect for children between the ages of two and four who are taking their first steps away from home. We are a co-educational Pre-School and Lower Prep, welcoming boys and girls up to Year 2, located in a beautiful setting with lots of outdoor space and school facilities. We benefit from access to the main school teaching staff who specialise in specific subjects and who come and teach our nursery school children French, PE, Music and Performing Arts/Dance as well as having access to our very own Forest School Leader and Forest School location in our own grounds in The Dell. We have two classes:
We like to consider the Nursery School as the beginning of a Manor House School education for children and we hope that you will want your child to progress through to our Reception Class and Lower Prep School.
Nursery for children aged 2-3 and
Kindergarten for children aged 3-4
How Does the Curriculum Help 2–4-Year-Olds Become Confident, Curious Learners?
We pride ourselves on providing a nurturing and welcoming start to school life, and we strive to create an environment specifically designed to meet the needs of each individual child. We offer an excellent curriculum providing first class Early Years teaching, along with specialist lessons in Performing Arts, French, Music and PE and Forest school sessions in our outdoor classroom, The Dell.
Parents often remark on the warm and friendly atmosphere in our Nursery and Pre-School, where each child’s developmental, social and emotional needs are met, and their progress is continually assessed. Our high staff ratio ensures the children are encouraged to learn at their own pace and reach their full potential.
All our learning activities are individually planned to keep children active and engaged, ensuring they develop the skills to move on to school as confident, motivated learners. These sessions have been created to take a structured and responsive approach to each child’s needs. We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework, alongside elements of Montessori practice, an approach that draws its principles from the natural development of the child. Our thriving Nursery School is a special place where children will be inspired to discover and learn as they play and make friends.
Ms Melanie Luke Director of Nursery Education and Mrs Redward Head of Key Stage 1 and 2, leads a team of fully qualified Early Years practitioners, all of whom are highly trained and enjoy building positive relationships with every child, delivering the best possible care and promoting excellent academic standards. Children are divided into small working groups, each with their own key member of staff.
Where Is the Nursery? Serving Families Across Bookham, Leatherhead and Cobham
Manor House Nursery School is based at Manor House Lane, Little Bookham, Leatherhead, Surrey, KT23 4EN, set within the grounds and facilities of Manor House School.
Our Nursery and Kindergarten sit in purpose-built accommodation alongside the Reception Class, with their own dedicated outdoor space and access to the wider seventeen acre site, including our Forest School in The Dell. Being part of the main school means your child is taught French, Music, PE and Performing Arts by the same subject specialists who teach further up the school, which is not something every nursery can offer.
We are a few minutes from Leatherhead, Fetcham, Effingham and Great and Little Bookham, and an easy drive from Cobham, Oxshott and the Horsleys. Please note that our school bus service, which covers Cobham, Leatherhead, Ashtead, Esher and many other areas, is available to pupils from age eight, so nursery children are brought in by parents. It is useful to know it is there for later years.
Is the Nursery Co-educational?
Yes. Our Nursery and Kindergarten are co-educational, welcoming both boys and girls from the age of two through to four.
We run two classes: Nursery for children aged two to three, and Kindergarten for children aged three to four. Boys and girls learn together throughout. Children are organised into small working groups, each with their own key member of staff, and our high staff ratios mean every child is known well and encouraged to learn at their own pace.
Our curriculum follows the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework alongside elements of Montessori practice, with activities planned individually so that each child stays active, engaged and builds the confidence to move on to school as a motivated learner. You can see how a typical week is structured on our Our Setting page.
If you would like to discuss a place for your son or daughter, our admissions team will be glad to help on 01372 457077 or at admissions@manorhouseschool.org, or you can visit our Nursery Admissions page.
How Can Parents Book a Visit to See the Nursery in Action?
We’d love for you to explore Manor House School for your family. To arrange a visit of this Nursery in Surrey and to see it in action, please book our next Open Day or contact the team at admissions@manorhouseschool.org.

pageCache.pageTitle: Upper Prep | Senior School | Manor House School
pageCache.text:
Upper Prep
YEAR 3
There is a general emphasis on developing greater independence in the first year of Key Stage 2 at Manor House. The majority of lessons are taught by the class teacher, with specialist teaching in Music, Drama, PE and French. In Science, the girls cover topics such as rocks and soils, forces and magnets, food and our bodies, and light. They also get the opportunity to grow their own plants and harvest them.
In Humanities, they study invaders and settlers, with a special focus on Celts and Romans, Anglo-Saxons and Vikings. The girls also investigate weather and climate across Europe, the Americas and the UK and explore the world’s tropical rain forests.
Class outings take place at least once per term throughout the year. Girls visit Fishbourne Roman Palace to gain an insight into life in Roman times, as well as the British Museum, to see the amazing artefacts related to this period in history.
The residential trip to Juniper Hall in May helps to extend the girls’ learning in Humanities and Science. This is a memorable visit as it is the pupils’ first experience of a residential trip and they get to spend one night away from home.
YEAR 4
In Year 4 at Manor House School our girls have a busy time working hard and thinking for themselves. We love to be creative and collaborative!
English, Mathematics, Science, Humanities, Art and PSHRSE are studied in their base class with their form teacher, Mrs Darlington. DT, French, Computing, PE, Music, Drama and RS are taught by specialist subject teachers.
In English, we enjoy all aspects of the written word. Writing and sharing poetry, creating stories and writing letters are just some of our activities. Reading is, of course, essential to all our work, so we read as much as we can to hone our skills.
Our Mathematics work takes place every morning, and we work in groups so that we can ensure that our work is tailored to suit the pace of our learning.
Our topics in Science include habitats and adaptation, so we can use our beautiful grounds at Manor House School to enhance aspects of this area of study. We also find out about teeth and eating and electricity. Plenty of hands-on work to inspire future scientists!
In Humanities, we study both historical and geographical topics. The study of natural disasters and their impact on our world forms part of the geographical work we do. We also study the reasons why people live where they do in both Guildford and Portsmouth.
The Tudors is a firm favourite with Year 4, as we incorporate two great trips to further our knowledge. One is to the National Portrait Gallery Tudor Room and the other to Hooke Court in Dorset. This is our two-night residential trip. While we are there, we do activities, some in full Tudor costume, which support our Tudor work, as well as encourage independence and self-confidence.
Y4 or Team 4D as we like to be called, love what we do every day!
YEAR 5
Girls in Year 5 of the Prep School at Manor House enjoy a wide and varied curriculum designed to stimulate independent thinking and a love of learning.
The majority of subjects are taught by the Form Teacher who is a primary specialist. This consistency allows the Form Teacher to build positive relationships within the form and across the Prep school. Girls are listened to and their views respected, supported and, when necessary, challenged within a strong, pastorally supportive environment.
Subject specialist teaching continues in French, Art, Music, Drama and PE and in Year 5 an extra language, Spanish, is also introduced.
Standards and expectations remain high in Year 5. We work with each girl with the aim that they all reach their full potential. We ensure that the girls are learning to be equipped to face the challenges and responsibilities of life. By instilling a sense of independence and resilience in the girls they become more confident to aim for greater success. The breadth and variety of topics taught in Year 5 also helps the girls to better understand the wider world from a literary, historical, geographical and ethical viewpoint.
The academic year begins with a team building, problem-solving and independence focused three-day residential to the beautiful centre of Sayers Croft in Ewhurst, Surrey. The activities, challenges and learning that takes place supports many areas of the Year 5 curriculum. This experience gives an opportunity for the girls to bond together, create memories and form new friendships.
Other trips include, a day visit to the South Downs Planetarium as part of their Science work on Earth and Space and a trip to the Victorian Schoolroom at Guildford Museum.
YEAR 6
Year 6 is a busy and exciting year full of opportunities for the girls to share in unforgettable experiences and to thoroughly enjoy their final year in the Prep Department. The girls are expected and encouraged to work hard and play hard, to be excellent role models in all aspects of Prep life and to support and lead activities wherever they can. House Leaders in the Preps assist in assemblies with House Rewards and work alongside the Senior House Captains to develop House Events and activities to further the House identity. School Council and Food Committee Representatives for Year 6 help to lead Prep School meetings and take ideas and recommendations for younger girls to Senior School meetings.
Following and extending the National Curriculum, English and Mathematics are taught in small ability groups set across the year ensuring that each girl’s learning is both challenged and supported as required. Computing lessons are delivered in the Senior ICT suite and Science lessons ensure that the girls have secure foundations and knowledge which will be built upon in the Seniors.
Humanities teaching includes studies of local and world Rivers and Mountains, World War Two and Japan. These projects are further enhanced through a Geography field trip in the Autumn and an immersive visit to Henley Fort during the Spring Term.
The girls are taught PE by specialist teachers and have the opportunity to participate in numerous match fixtures across the year both as representatives of their House and the School.
Our Year 6 Residential Visit to PGL on the Isle of Wight in the Summer Term involves a range of exciting challenges, including Water Sports and team activities. This trip is a great opportunity to practice skills of independence and personal organisation which we nurture and develop throughout the year. Specialist teachers deliver Music and Drama lessons and all girls value and enjoy the experience of singing at the O2 as part of the Young Voices concert. The girls in Year 6 take the lead roles in the Prep Production which is always a highlight and rounds off an exciting, challenging and inspiring year which prepares them well for their next phase in the Senior School.

Facilities and Venue Hire
Outstanding Facilities
Set within 17 acres of beautiful grounds in Bookham, Surrey, Manor House School offers an exceptional learning environment where pupils are inspired to thrive academically, creatively and personally. Nestled within Surrey’s picturesque commuter belt, the School combines the charm and character of a historic setting with outstanding modern facilities designed to nurture curiosity, confidence and achievement.
At the heart of the campus stands the magnificent 17th-century Manor House, surrounded by formal gardens, extensive playing fields, a wildlife area and orchard. Recognised by The Telegraph as one of the UK’s most beautiful schools, Manor House School provides a truly unique setting where heritage and innovation sit side by side.
Our bright, well-equipped classrooms are complemented by an impressive range of specialist facilities that ignite creativity and inspire a love of learning. These include a purpose-built Art and Textiles Studio with kiln facilities, a dedicated Music Room, a mirrored Drama Studio, and a dedicated Dance Studio where pupils can develop their performance skills, confidence and creativity.
Innovation and discovery are encouraged through our modern STEM Centre, providing exciting opportunities for pupils to explore science, technology, engineering and mathematics through hands-on learning. The School also benefits from a fully equipped Science Laboratory for Prep pupils, a modern ICT Suite and a spacious Food Technology Suite with individual practical workstations, enabling children to develop independence and confidence in a professional-style kitchen environment.
At the heart of the Manor House is our welcoming Library and Learning Space, offering a calm and inspiring environment for reading, research and independent study. This much-loved hub encourages a lifelong love of books while supporting pupils in developing strong literacy and critical-thinking skills.
Our versatile facilities include the Elizabeth Green Hall, which serves as a sports hall, theatre and assembly venue, alongside the Arcot Hall within the Manor House itself, providing additional flexible space for performances, celebrations, events and community activities.
As a leading independent school in Bookham, Surrey, Manor House School is proud of its extensive sporting facilities. These include an open-air heated swimming pool, five floodlit tennis and netball courts, hockey and football pitches, cricket nets and an athletics track, providing excellent opportunities for pupils to develop teamwork, resilience and a lifelong love of sport.
The Dell is our unique Forest School setting, a secluded valley nestled among mature trees and designed to support adventurous outdoor learning. With purpose-built shelters, seating areas and space to explore the natural environment, The Dell encourages children to build resilience, foster collaboration and develop a deeper connection with the world around them.
Many of our outstanding facilities are also available through our school facilities hire programme, making Manor House School a sought-after venue in Surrey for sports clubs, community groups, educational organisations and local events.
FUNCTIONS AND WEDDING HIRE
We offer exclusive use of our beautiful Grade II listed Queen Anne building and landscaped grounds for weddings or special occasions.
This is possible at the week-ends during term-time and during the School holidays.
We host sports tournaments on our courts and field too.
Local theatre and dance groups also use Elizabeth Green Hall for shows and the Bookham Belles WI regularly use Arcot Hall for their meetings.
Local clubs have utilised our Food & Nutrition Room, and Art Room too.
Contact us for more information about hiring Manor House as a venue, via email, to tgamble@manorhouseschool.org for more information about venue hire.

pageCache.text:
Our History
Over 100 years ago, Manor House School began as two small classes run by Miss Green and Miss Wheeler in Sidmouth, Devon in 1920. They joined forces and “The Beehive” was born.
By 1929, the two ladies decided to move to Surrey because they wished to branch out into boarding, as a Private Girls’ School, and it was felt that Devon was too far for London families to travel. For seven years they rented Mickleham Hall in Dorking, but in 1937 the school moved to Bookham after Miss Green purchased the Manor House at auction. Manor House School has been settled here ever since as an Independent School in Surrey.
The Queen Anne house was built in 1710 but had been empty for some time when the school moved in. A new wing, Arcot Hall, was added and the gardens were tamed. In 1939 Miss Wheeler died suddenly and Miss Green carried on as sole headmistress until 1965.
In 1961, the school became an educational trust. Miss Green retired to Meadow Cottage in the grounds in 1965 and remained an interested observer until her death on 10 August 1978. She and Miss Wheeler are buried in All Saints Church, Little Bookham, next door to the school and they are remembered on ‘Founders Day’.
“Manor House School has educated many girls (and boys) since first opening in 1920. Today, our growing community of pupils and staff were excited to have recognised 100 years in 2020. We offer a high quality, well rounded education where girls develop a love of learning, achieve academic excellence and become confident and happy individuals. The School is filled with energy and passion on a day-to-day basis and I never cease to be amazed by the talent, ambition and courage of our pupils. Our founders, Miss Green and Miss Wheeler, who were two very inspirational and forward thinking women, would be very proud of their legacy” Tracey Fantham, Headteacher.
Manor House School has expanded over the years, adding Main Block, Mason Block, the Nursery, Art/Textiles block and Music, Drama and Home Economics facilities.

pageCache.text:
Spiritual Life
Manor House School is an Independent School and Nursery in Surrey which welcomes pupils of all faiths. We are Christian in tradition and aim to foster Christian values of spiritual awareness, understanding and respect for others and this is expressed in the way pupils throughout the school treat one another.
All our pupils join in regular assemblies within school, which lie at the heart of our life together as a community. Year groups also take it in turns to enjoy a church service in the beautiful Saxon church, All Saints, adjacent to the school in Bookham, and whole school services are special occasions.
Throughout the curriculum, space is given in many subjects for questioning, reflection and self-awareness. All religions are explored in Religious Studies with a particular emphasis on Christianity. A Christian Union is available as an extra-curricular activity.
